project.commit_note: The staged reproducing checkout under `_work/src/fluent-bit` is commit `dbe29a1a77b544b9e1b39e9b32e151ac22c6874e`, while sample metadata names `f38dd464371d73421fbf0aac9435d1ca936996ed`. On the crashing path, the staged `lib/onigmo/regparse.c` and `lib/onigmo/regenc.c` are line-identical to that metadata commit, and the saved ASan frames (`src/flb_env.c:181`, `src/flb_parser.c:442/506/559/870`, `src/flb_regex.c:78/108`, `lib/onigmo/regparse.c:1473/6584/6905/6938/6987/7032`, `lib/onigmo/regcomp.c:5754/5982`) match the staged checkout. The fix commit `9cc2ff55a146b2b3e8c321a87920c0d39a2b2ba6` then adds the missing post-`PFETCH` bounds guard in `lib/onigmo/regparse.c`.

bug_description.normalized: The staged 724-byte witness is written to disk by `config_random_fuzzer` and then parsed by `flb_parser_conf_file()` in the staged checkout `dbe29a1a77b544b9e1b39e9b32e151ac22c6874e`. In that witness, line 4 is `[P]S]`; `read_config()` stops that header at the first `]`, so `flb_cf_section_create(cf, buf + 1, end - 1)` receives the one-byte name `P`, which `get_section_type()` classifies as `FLB_CF_PARSER`. The classic config parser then captures the first-byte `L` from parser-property lines as the indent token and strips it from later lines, so line 8 `Lregex 11 c7 c7 c7 2e 53 2f 2a ec` and line 9 `Lformat regex` are copied into that same parser section as `regex` and `format` properties. `parser_conf_file()` later retrieves `format == "regex"` and the 9-byte `regex` value; `flb_env_var_translate()` computes `len = strlen(value) == 9`, and `flb_sds_create_size(9)` allocates the 26-byte SDS region that ASan later reports (16-byte header + 9-byte payload + NUL). `flb_parser_create()` classifies the parser as `FLB_PARSER_REGEX`, `flb_regex_create()` forwards the SDS to `str_to_regex()`, and `str_to_regex()` passes the logical UTF-8 span `[pattern, pattern + 9)` into `onig_new()`. Inside Onigmo, the trailing byte `0xec` is an incomplete 3-byte UTF-8 leader, so `onigenc_mbclen_approximate()` returns an approximate width of 3, `fetch_token()` advances `p` past `end` via `PFETCH(c)` without the fixed commit's added `if (p > end)` guard, and `parse_exp()` immediately calls `node_new_str(tok->backp, *src)`. The copy block in `onig_node_str_cat()` then performs the observed `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 3` on a token span that straddles the 9-byte payload end inside that 26-byte SDS allocation, matching `onig_node_str_cat -> parse_exp -> parse_branch`. Stage 02 did not execute fixed-image validation; the patch is used only to identify the missing source-level obligation.

source.description: Source. `read_config()` consumes the attacker-controlled section header and materializes the parser-section object that later accumulates the `regex` and `format` properties used on the vulnerable path.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_46049/poc` is 724 bytes with SHA-256 `20e6cc523fe97217c98f49fec1952ae89d3959b5ebc01f015c83b0f0fe6905be`. Its line 4 is `[P]S]`, so `char_search(buf, ']', len)` stops at the first `]` and line 546 passes `buf + 1` with `end - 1 == 1` into `flb_cf_section_create()`. That one-byte name `P` is enough for `get_section_type()` to classify the new section as `FLB_CF_PARSER`, and later line 8 / line 9 bytes are copied into this same section before the crashing `parser_conf_file()` retrievals.
source.note: This is the first project statement that turns the witness into vulnerability-relevant parser state: a live `current_section` linked into `cf->parsers`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `fetch_token()` records the token start and then advances `p` by `enclen(enc, p, end)` through `PFETCH(c)` without checking whether the resulting pointer escaped the logical regex end.
root_cause.note: For the crashing 9-byte UTF-8 pattern, the final byte `0xec` yields an approximate width of 3 while only one byte remains before `end`, so `PFETCH(c)` moves `p` past the logical regex end. Fixed commit `9cc2ff55a146b2b3e8c321a87920c0d39a2b2ba6` repairs this exact omission by inserting `if (p > end) return ONIGERR_PREMATURE_END_OF_CHAR_CLASS;` immediately after `PFETCH(c);`.

sink.description: Sink. The string-node copy block inside `onig_node_str_cat()` trusts the token span `[s, end)` and copies `end - s` bytes from it into node storage.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports the crashing project frame as `onig_node_str_cat` and the call chain `onig_node_str_cat -> parse_exp -> parse_branch`. The saved trace does not symbolize the exact copy line inside the function, so this sink anchors the shared copy block at lines 1378-1405. On the staged witness, `str_to_regex()` passed a 9-byte logical payload inside a 26-byte SDS allocation, and the overrun token span extends beyond that 9-byte end. `onig_strcpy(..., s, end)` therefore performs the observed `READ of size 3` on a copy that straddles the payload boundary inside the SDS allocation.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant derived value is the approximate multibyte width returned for a truncated UTF-8 tail. This helper turns a `NEEDMORE` result into a positive length larger than the bytes still available before `end`, and `fetch_token()` later uses that returned width as `enclen(enc, p, end)`.
tainted_value_origin.note: Under `ONIG_ENCODING_UTF8`, `p` can only step past `end` in `PFETCH(c)` if this branch converts a truncated sequence into an approximate positive width.

parser_admitted.description: After `parser_conf_file()` retrieves `format == regex`, `flb_parser_create()` admits the attacker-controlled `regex` property into the vulnerable regex compiler path by calling `flb_regex_create(p_regex)`.

fine_trace.note: Source. On witness line 4 `[P]S]`, `char_search()` stops at the first `]`, so this passes the one-byte name `P` into `flb_cf_section_create()`. `get_section_type()` therefore classifies the new section as `FLB_CF_PARSER` and links it into `cf->parsers`, making later properties on this section reachable from `parser_conf_file()`.

The first property line under this section causes `indent` to become the one-byte string `"L"` because the loop increments `i` once before testing blanks. When later lines 8 and 9 begin with `Lregex` and `Lformat`, `check_indent()` matches that same prefix and `indent_len = 1` strips the leading `L`, so the effective keys start at `regex` and `format`.

On witness line 8 `Lregex 11 c7 c7 c7 2e 53 2f 2a ec`, step 2 makes `key == "regex"` and `val_len == 9`. `flb_cf_property_add()` duplicates those 9 bytes into `current_section->properties`, so the parser section now carries the exact regex payload that later reaches Onigmo.

On witness line 9 `Lformat regex`, the same parsing logic stores `key == "format"` with value `"regex"` in the same section. This is the load-bearing dispatch string later used to select the regex parser path.
When `parser_conf_file()` iterates the parser section from step 1, this retrieves the step-4 property as the SDS string `"regex"`.

This retrieves the step-3 property and sends it through `get_parser_key()` to `flb_env_var_translate()`. For the staged witness, `strlen(value) == 9`, so `flb_sds_create_size(9)` allocates the 26-byte SDS region that the saved ASan allocation stack later identifies as the overread source object.
The step-5 string compares equal to `"regex"`, so the new parser is classified as `FLB_PARSER_REGEX`. This decision is the control precondition for the `flb_regex_create(p_regex)` block.
Because step 7 selected `FLB_PARSER_REGEX`, the line-206 `if (p->type == FLB_PARSER_REGEX)` gate is taken and this call forwards the step-6 SDS as `p_regex` into the regex compiler.

For the staged payload `11 c7 c7 c7 2e 53 2f 2a ec`, `strlen(pattern) == 9`. Because the value neither begins nor ends with `'/'`, `start` stays at `pattern` and `end` becomes `pattern + 9` before `onig_new()` receives the logical UTF-8 span.

At the trailing payload byte `0xec`, UTF-8 precise decode needs two more continuation bytes. This helper therefore turns `NEEDMORE(2)` into `enclen(enc, p, end) == 3`, which is larger than the single byte still available before the logical `end`.

Root cause. `fetch_token()` records the token start and then advances `p += enclen(enc, p, end)` through `PFETCH(c)`. On the crashing token, step 10 supplied `enclen == 3` even though only the final payload byte remained, so `p` moves from the last regex byte to `end + 2`. The vulnerable file does not check `if (p > end)` here; fixed commit `9cc2ff55a146b2b3e8c321a87920c0d39a2b2ba6` adds exactly `if (p > end) return ONIGERR_PREMATURE_END_OF_CHAR_CLASS;` after `PFETCH(c);`.

After step 11, `fetch_token()` publishes the advanced cursor as the token end. The exported `*src` now lies two bytes past the true 9-byte `pattern_end`, while `tok->backp` still points at the final in-bounds byte.

`parse_exp()` trusts the span `[tok->backp, *src)` as valid string data and materializes it immediately with `node_new_str()`. The saved ASan crash stack names this exact call site directly above `parse_branch`.

Sink. `onig_node_str_cat()` computes `addlen = end - s` from the step-13 span and then copies `[s, end)` through `onig_strcpy(..., s, end)`. Because that span extends beyond the 9-byte regex payload inside the 26-byte SDS from step 6, this copy produces the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 3` in `onig_node_str_cat -> parse_exp -> parse_branch`.

allocation_context.note: The saved ASan allocation stack shows the source region is allocated through `flb_sds_create_size(len)` when step 6 retrieves the `regex` property via `get_parser_key()`. In the staged witness `len == 9`, so the reported 26-byte region is the SDS allocation that contains the 9-byte regex payload, not a 26-byte logical pattern string.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: function-level: the saved ASan trace reports `onig_node_str_cat` as the crashing project frame but omits the exact copy line inside that function; fine-trace step 14 models the copy block at lines 1378-1405.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation stack identifies the same 26-byte SDS allocation containing the 9-byte regex payload materialized in step 6 from the step-3 `regex` property; the root cause is the later token-end overrun in steps 10-11, not the allocation itself.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The saved stack `flb_env_var_translate -> get_parser_key -> flb_parser_create -> flb_regex_create -> str_to_regex -> onig_new -> onig_compile -> parse_exp -> parse_branch -> onig_node_str_cat` matches fine-trace steps 6-14 after the earlier source-grounded config-parser materialization at steps 1-5; the only unsymbolized detail is the exact copy line inside `onig_node_str_cat`.

format.name: Fluent Bit parser configuration
format.contract: The staged witness must still parse line 4 `[P]S]` as a parser section and strip the one-byte `L` indent from line 8 `Lregex 11 c7 c7 c7 2e 53 2f 2a ec` and line 9 `Lformat regex`, so the same section yields `format == "regex"` and the same 9-byte regex payload. `flb_parser_create()` must therefore compile that value under `ONIG_ENCODING_UTF8`; the final byte `0xec` then causes `fetch_token()` to advance `*src` two bytes past the 9-byte `pattern_end`, and `onig_node_str_cat()` copies the resulting 3-byte span across that boundary.
